messages:
alex: hitting flakiness in our sample Android app. Retrofit + OkHttp auth flow seems to loop when refresh token is used during background sync. 401 -> refresh -> still 401 -> repeated retries until worker times out. anyone seen this?

nina: yep, familiar. quick checklist: are you using the same OkHttpClient for the refresh call? that often causes re-entrant authenticators.

alex: we are. sample code: 
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator())
  .addInterceptor { chain ->
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${TokenStore.current}")
      .build()
    chain.proceed(req)
  }
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .build()

val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder()
  .client(client)
  .baseUrl("https://api.redwood.example/")
  .build()
```
we do the token refresh synchronously inside TokenAuthenticator.

prateek: that is exactly the pattern that creates recursion. Authenticator triggers refresh, which makes an HTTP call using the same client -> server returns 401 for the refresh -> authenticator invoked again -> loop. Fix: use a separate client without authenticator for the refresh call.

jen: additionally, interceptor placement matters. application interceptors run for both original and follow-up requests but they don't see network-level modifications made by an authenticator on a follow-up. For adding Authorization headers to retried requests prefer a network interceptor or build the header into the Request returned by authenticate().

alex: we relied on reading token from disk in the interceptor, so moving to network interceptor makes me nervous (disk IO on network thread). any suggestions?

nina: options: 1) keep the interceptor but read token from an in-memory cache populated at app start / on refresh, avoid disk on network thread; 2) use a lightweight dedicated refresh client that uses OkHttp without interceptors; 3) in authenticate() return a Request with the header so OkHttp doesn't need the interceptor for the follow-up.

prateek: code example we use in SDK samples:
```kotlin
val refreshClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(null)
  .addInterceptor { chain -> chain.proceed(chain.request()) }
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .callTimeout(8, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()

class TokenAuthenticator(private val refreshClient: OkHttpClient): Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    if (response.request.url.encodedPath.contains("/oauth/token")) return null // don't recurse
    val newToken = runBlocking { refreshToken(refreshClient) }
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
      .build()
  }
}
```
that pattern avoids reentrancy and also avoids touching disk on the network thread if you cache token in memory.

jen: also consider disabling retryOnConnectionFailure for clients that perform auth-sensitive operations if you want more deterministic behavior. set callTimeout and readTimeout so WorkManager tasks fail fast and can be retried by the app logic instead of OkHttp's internal retries.

alex: good call. any Android-specific ProGuard or coroutine adapter gotchas?

nina: ProGuard rarely affects this flow unless you obfuscate a custom callback adapter. For coroutine adapters, ensure you cancel Retrofit calls if the coroutine scope is cancelled (WorkManager stop). Otherwise the authenticator block might keep the process alive.

prateek: one more: OkHttp older versions had subtle differences in when authenticators are invoked relative to redirects. Our SDK README should document the recommended pattern and provide a helper to create the refresh client. Right now samples show the naive pattern and it's causing support tickets.

alex: can someone open an MR to update the Android sample app and SDK README? I'll record the reproducer and add logs.

ci-bot: created MR 4391 to update android samples, include TokenAuthenticator example, and add CI test using MockWebServer (https://git.internal/redwood/mr/4391) :white_check_mark:

jen: assign to @prateek for tests, @nina for README, @alex for reproducer. thanks all.

alex: thanks! i'll also add a note about network vs application interceptors so other teams don't accidentally hit this.
